1980s: Dynamic semantics / file change semantics / DRT
Cognitive linguistics / Women, Fire, and Dangerous Things
2010s: Distributional semantics at scale (word2vec, GloVe, BERT, GPT)

tools.name: Theory of Descriptions
tools.phenomenon: denotation failure ('the present King of France is bald')
tools.mechanism: rewrite definite descriptions as existential quantifications; preserves bivalence by making such sentences false rather than gappy
tools.limit: preserves bivalence by stipulation; many linguists later preferred Strawson's gap analysis as more faithful to ordinary usage

tools.name: Sense / Reference distinction
tools.phenomenon: two terms with same reference but different cognitive content (Hesperus / Phosphorus); also raised proto-presuppositional concerns (e.g. denotation failure of 'the present King of France') though without formalizing them in the modern Strawson/Heim sense
tools.mechanism: two-level meaning: sense (mode of presentation) + reference (object)
tools.limit: binary distinction; cited here mainly for sense/reference, not for a fully developed presupposition theory (which traces more directly to Strawson 1950 and Heim 1983); does not handle context-conditioned reference shifts at the granularity LLMs do

tools.name: Presupposition / truth-value gaps
tools.phenomenon: sentences with failed presuppositions ('the King of France is bald' when there is no king)
tools.mechanism: third truth-value (gap, undefined, or 'neither true nor false')
tools.limit: handles presupposition specifically; not a general theory of tralseness

tools.name: Three-valued logics (Kleene, Bochvar)
tools.phenomenon: presupposition failure, partial functions, undefined values
tools.mechanism: third truth-value with strong/weak connective tables
tools.limit: specifically for undefinedness; does not address polysemy, vagueness, or definitional bistability

tools.name: Two Dogmas of Empiricism
tools.phenomenon: the analytic-synthetic distinction breaks down on examination
tools.mechanism: argument that meaning and fact cannot be cleanly separated; web-of-belief holism
tools.limit: philosophical critique; does not provide a positive formal alternative

tools.name: Distributional structure
tools.phenomenon: lexical meaning as patterns of co-occurrence
tools.mechanism: meaning as distribution over linguistic contexts ('you shall know a word by the company it keeps')
tools.limit: originally informal; took five decades to become computationally tractable (word2vec 2013)

tools.name: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
tools.phenomenon: scientific terms shift meaning across paradigms (mass, species, gene)
tools.mechanism: paradigms as systems of meaning; incommensurability across paradigm shifts
tools.limit: largely historical / philosophical; not a formal semantics

tools.name: Fuzzy sets / fuzzy semantics
tools.phenomenon: vague predicates with no sharp boundary ('tall', 'red', 'old')
tools.mechanism: graded membership in [0,1]; truth-degrees rather than truth-values
tools.limit: gradient-based; less natural for discrete bistability and for combinatorial tralseness

tools.name: Prototype theory in linguistics
tools.phenomenon: category membership is graded; prototypical members vs peripheral ('robin' vs 'penguin' as 'bird')
tools.mechanism: categories defined by similarity to prototype, not by necessary-and-sufficient conditions
tools.limit: psychological focus; less developed as a formal semantic system

tools.name: Supervaluation for vagueness
tools.phenomenon: Sorites paradox; vague predicates
tools.mechanism: truth = true on all admissible precisifications; preserves classical tautologies despite vagueness
tools.limit: preserves bivalence at the cost of higher-order vagueness; Williamson 1994 critiques the framework's stability

tools.name: Possible-worlds semantics for modality
tools.phenomenon: counterfactuals, possibility, necessity
tools.mechanism: truth relative to a world; modals quantify over accessible worlds
tools.limit: world-relative bivalence; does not directly address polysemy or definitional bistability

tools.name: Scalar implicature
tools.phenomenon: 'some' implicates 'not all'; pragmatic strengthening of literal content
tools.mechanism: Gricean-style maxim-driven inference layered on top of bivalent semantic content
tools.limit: two-layer architecture (semantics bivalent, pragmatics adds content); preserves bivalent core

tools.name: Scorekeeping / contextualism
tools.phenomenon: truth-conditions depend on conversational context (epistemic standards, comparison classes)
tools.mechanism: context as an index that shifts truth-conditions; conversational scoreboard updated by participants
tools.limit: preserves bivalent truth at each context-index; the index is the parameter, the truth is bivalent given the index

tools.name: Dynamic semantics / file change semantics / DRT
tools.phenomenon: anaphora across sentences; cross-sentential dynamics; donkey sentences
tools.mechanism: meaning as context-update potential; sentences update an information state rather than mapping to truth-values directly
tools.limit: TAG IS CONTESTABLE: tagged constitutive here because the headline move is meaning-as-update rather than meaning-as-truth, but most dynamic-semantics frameworks still preserve truth/satisfaction conditions relative to contexts and so could equally well be tagged corrective; this URB takes the constitutive reading but reasonable interpreters would tag it differently; also the philosophical ramification (meaning-as-update vs meaning-as-truth) was not foregrounded by the field as a foundational shift

tools.name: Cognitive linguistics / Women, Fire, and Dangerous Things
tools.phenomenon: embodied meaning, frames, image schemas, conceptual metaphor
tools.mechanism: meaning as embodied conceptual structure; explicitly opposed to truth-conditional bivalent semantics
tools.limit: treated by formal-semantics mainstream as a competing paradigm rather than as a foundational corrective; institutional integration has been partial

tools.name: Demonstratives / indexicality
tools.phenomenon: 'I', 'here', 'now', 'this' have context-dependent reference
tools.mechanism: two-level semantics: character (function from context to content) + content (proposition); preserves bivalent truth at each context
tools.limit: preserves bivalent truth-conditions per context; the tralseness is in the context-dependence, not in the truth-value itself

tools.name: Vagueness (Williamson)
tools.phenomenon: Sorites; epistemicism; survey of supervaluation, fuzzy logic, contextualism
tools.mechanism: epistemicist defense of bivalence: vague predicates have sharp boundaries we don't know
tools.limit: explicitly defends bivalence at the cost of an unknowable sharp boundary; the most thorough modern defense of the bivalent-core architecture against vagueness pressure

tools.name: Verbal Disputes
tools.phenomenon: philosophical disputes that hinge on definitional choice rather than substantive disagreement
tools.mechanism: method of elimination: strike out the contested term; if substantive disagreement vanishes, the dispute was merely verbal
tools.limit: diagnostic / methodological; does not propose a unified semantics for definitional bistability beyond the diagnostic move

tools.name: Inquisitive semantics
tools.phenomenon: questions and assertions in a unified framework; meaning as proposing alternatives
tools.mechanism: propositions as sets of possibilities; both questions and assertions express semantic content
tools.limit: unifies questions and assertions; less developed for polysemy and definitional bistability specifically

tools.name: Distributional semantics at scale (word2vec, GloVe, BERT, GPT)
tools.phenomenon: context-conditioned meaning representation at industrial scale
tools.tralse_type: all (distributional, context, polysemy, implicature emerge in the geometry)
tools.mechanism: high-dimensional vector embeddings + attention; meaning as context-conditioned predictive distribution
tools.limit: foundationally non-bivalent; opaque to symbolic analysis; the philosophical implications for semantics have been noticed but not unified into a foundational shift in linguistic theory

interpretation: Linguistics and philosophy of language have at least 20 substantial tools / theories addressing tralse-like phenomena, spanning 1890s to 2010s. Of these, this catalog tags 10 as constitutive (default / foundational) and 10 as corrective (patches to a bivalent core), with 1 explicitly marked as having a contested tag (reasonable interpreters would classify them differently). The constitutive/corrective tags are INTERPRETIVE LABELS, not objective measurements: another reasonable observer could shift several items between buckets and the apparent 50/50 split is a function of which items are included and how the borderline ones are tagged, not a quantitative finding. The corrective tools are mostly in the dominant formal-semantics mainstream (Russell's theory of descriptions, Kleene/Bochvar three-valued logics, supervaluation, possible-worlds modality, scalar implicature, contextualism, Kaplanian indexicality, Williamson's epistemicism). The constitutive tools are mostly outside the formal mainstream (Quine, Harris/Firth distributional, Kuhn, fuzzy sets, prototype theory, dynamic semantics [contested], cognitive linguistics, Chalmers' verbal-disputes diagnostic, inquisitive semantics, modern distributional / LLM-based semantics). This is the structural observation behind URB #816: the technical machinery exists, but the constitutive vs corrective polarity is split across the field, and the formal-mainstream commitment to bivalent-core-with-patches has been the institutionally dominant frame. TI Sigma's specific PROPOSED contribution is foundational reframing (invert the polarity, make tralseness the default) plus unification of the philosophical ramifications — NOT new technical mechanisms, and NOT a settled result; the proposal itself is a hypothesis to be argued for.
